headline.undefined_note: a member whose compared cell did not install is UNDEFINED, not flat: its numbers are not evidence for the dosage account and are never counted with the flat lines
headline.verdict_change_note: a verdict that changes between the narrow-span pilot run and this run reflects a different injected width and, for most members, a member that could not be read at all before; it is not two measurements of the same quantity disagreeing
headline.recovery: of the members whose one-sighting reference cell failed its probe screen in the narrow-span pilot run, this is how many install at full width
headline.multiplicity: Each member's verdict reads four bootstrap intervals -- the 6-vs-1 difference and three adjacent pairs -- across seven members, 28 interval decisions in all, and no correction is applied. The rule is asymmetric: REPETITION or SPREADING_COSTS needs ONE interval to exclude zero (about 0.35 spurious calls expected across the panel at 5 percent), while MIXED_NON_MONOTONE triggers on any of three (about one expected). So a panel count of 1 in either category is not read as a per-model finding, and the report says so wherever such a count appears.
headline.rule: STATED BEFORE THIS RUN PRODUCED A NUMBER, because changing a rule after seeing results is exactly the move that needs to be visible. PRIMARY: each compared cell must beat all 24 norm-matched random directions on the PROBE -- the first lever run forced self-report margin, read from a probe turn appended to the same frozen conditioning ids under the same span mask, ranked first among itself and the 24 -- and the REFERENCE cell (one sighting) must additionally show its own effect on the choice margin with a bootstrap interval excluding zero (its full-n differenced-margin slope). The reference cell is NOT required to outrank the 24 random directions on the choice margin. Rationale: the strength pilot run rule as written required the reference cell to be significant on the very quantity the comparison measures, which is close to requiring the answer in advance and discards a weak-but-real reference; the permissive rule it actually implemented let a cell that ranked last of 25 on the choice margin carry a 'repetition' reading. TWO ALTERNATE READINGS are computed and reported beside the primary for all seven members: STRICT, both screens rank first for every compared cell (the strength pilot run plan as written), and PERMISSIVE, either screen (the strength pilot run implementation).
headline.reading: per model, never pooled: the panel line is 'in N of the 7 models we tested'

recorded.source: <run id> results/analysis262.json members.olmo_32b.under_relative.cells.e6_k1.slope_full_n, as recorded in src/prior267.py; the narrow-span pilot run re-measured the same cell under the same rule and reproduced it to every digit

anchor.estimand: One cell keeps the strength pilot run span rule and omits the priming turn: OLMo-2-32B at six sightings and full strength. Its full-n slope must reproduce the strength pilot run own measured +0.5840 within a factor of two in both directions. That is what proves the span change is the only difference between the runs. The corrected-geometry cells CANNOT serve as a reproduction check, because their geometry is what changed; the shift between the legacy cell and the corrected six-sighting cell is measured and reported rather than gated on.

attribution.claim_supported: the reference cell is readable under this geometry, which is what the constant-total row needs
attribution.claim_not_supported: that per-sighting WIDTH is why. At one sighting, per-sighting width and total injected positions are the same number, so no cell in this run or in the narrow-span pilot run separates them -- and the narrow-span pilot run own ranks point the other way: at an identical 15-token width its e2_khalf, e3_kthird, e6_kl2, e6_ksixth cells ranked 1 while its one-sighting cell ranked 3, so the cell that failed was the one with the FEWEST TOTAL injected positions, not the thinnest sighting
attribution.criterion: RECORDED BEFORE THE PANEL RAN. If OLMo-2-32B's one-sighting reference cell installs here and did not in the narrow-span pilot run, that shows the reference cell is readable under this geometry -- which is what the row needs -- but it does NOT show that per-sighting width is why. the narrow-span pilot run own ranks rule that story out: at an identical 15-token width, its e1_k1 cell ranked 3 of 25 while e2_khalf, e3_kthird, e6_kl2 and e6_ksixth all ranked 1. The cell that failed the screen was the one with the FEWEST TOTAL injected positions, not the thinnest per sighting. At one sighting the two quantities are the same number, so neither the narrow-span pilot run nor this run can separate them, and the recovery is reported as 'the reference cell is now readable', never as 'wider sightings are what fixed it'.

recovery_gate.criterion: The wide rule ADDS injected positions back, and the question is whether that is enough for the cells the narrow-span pilot run could not read. Four cells run with their full 24-direction floor before the panel spends anything: OLMo-2-32B's one-sighting reference cell (probe rank 3 of 25 in the narrow-span pilot run) and Qwen2.5-32B's (rank 9), and the thinnest cell in the design at both members. Each must install on the probe. OLMo's reference cell is the one that decides the recovery claim; if it still fails, OLMo is reported INSTRUMENT_LIMITED_AT_FULL_WIDTH, which is a finding about the instrument and never a null about the model, and the panel continues for the other six members.

recorded.criterion: the bridge cell must NOT install on the probe (rank > 1), reproducing the narrow-span pilot run failure on the identical cell, and its slope must sit within a factor of two of the narrow-span pilot run. A bridge that installs, or one whose slope moves by more than that, means the two runs differ by something other than the priming turn and the span rule, and the recovery comparison is void.

attribution.means_what: the two cells differ in per-sighting width, in total injected positions (they have one sighting each, so those are the same number) and in the priming turn. The bridge shows the geometry change is what moved the screen INSIDE this run; it does not isolate width from total positions or from the priming context

width_bridge.means: the thin geometry fails on this cell inside this run too, so the wide cell's success is a geometry effect measured within one run rather than across two
width_bridge.criterion: One cell keeps the narrow-span pilot run thin rule and omits the priming turn: OLMo-2-32B at one sighting, full strength, same seeds. It must NOT install on the probe -- reproducing the narrow-span pilot run rank 3 of 25 on the identical cell -- and its slope must sit within a factor of two of the narrow-span pilot run +0.5951. That makes 'widening recovered this model' a comparison between two cells of THIS run rather than a comparison across runs, which is the only way to make it while the token stream differs. A bridge cell that installs, or whose slope moves more than that, voids the recovery comparison and is reported as such.

mistral24b.caveat: this member's sighting is only 11 tokens wide, 2 more than the narrow-span pilot run, because its template's whole later-turn delta is that short once the preamble moves to the priming turn. The widening therefore does NOT remove a detection-floor account of a fall or a null here

width_gain.criterion: RECORDED BEFORE THE PANEL RAN. The widening is not uniform across members, and in one member it is nearly nothing. Per-sighting width goes from 15 to 23 tokens on OLMo-2-32B (1.533x), 13 to 18 on Qwen2.5-32B, Gemma-3-27B and Llama-3.1-8B (1.385x), 17 to 22 on both Qwen3s (1.294x) -- and 9 to 11 on Mistral-24B (1.222x), because Mistral's whole later-turn delta is 11 tokens once its 176-token preamble lands on the priming turn instead. the strength pilot run 96-token Mistral figure was that preamble, not a wide sighting. So for Mistral this run adds two positions per sighting, and a fall or a null there still cannot be separated from a detection floor; its row is reported with that caveat attached whatever the screens say. The other six members gain 29 to 53 percent more positions per sighting.

stream_identity.note: every session of every cell renders under one frozen template clock, and cells that share a span rule and a sighting count must be byte-identical at every seed. This replaces cross-run byte identity, which the priming turn gives up by design.

design_check.note: the corrected geometry makes the delivered total equal by construction and stage 1 refused above 3 percent, so this is a second, redundant guard; a negative offset would mean the six-sighting end delivered less push and so would favour reading the difference as 'spreading costs'

ladder.curvature_note: quadratic term of log slope against log per-sighting strength. Zero is a pure power law; NEGATIVE bends away at the thin end, which is the shape a threshold below the thinnest cell would produce. Three points fix a quadratic exactly, so this has no residual degrees of freedom; the interval is a parametric draw from each cell's own bootstrap interval treating the cells as independent, which they are not, so it is wider than the truth
ladder.note: three per-position strengths at the SAME six sightings. This is the axis the constant-total row's residual lives on, so it is the calibration for the magnitude adjustment as well as a result in its own right

row_reading.criterion:
Per member, on the constant-total row, with every compared cell required to have installed under the primary installation rule. A pair COUNTS AS MOVING only when its raw difference AND its magnitude-adjusted difference both exclude zero in the same direction. The direction is read off the difference itself -- spreading the same total over six sightings raises the effect (REPETITION) or lowers it (SPREADING_COSTS). the strength pilot run wrote the same rule as 'the same direction as the full-strength 6-vs-1 difference', which was equivalent there because that difference was positive in all seven of its members; stated directly here so the label cannot invert if a member's full-strength pair comes out flat or negative, and whether it does is reported beside the verdict.
TOTAL_MAGNITUDE  -- the 6-vs-1 difference's CI contains zero, no adjacent pair moves, AND that CI also EXCLUDES the full-strength 6-vs-1 difference in this member, which is the difference the dosage account predicts if the total were what mattered. Spreading the same total over more sightings then demonstrably changes nothing.
TIE_UNDERPOWERED -- the same tie WITHOUT that equivalence: the interval still admits a dosage-sized difference, so the member is unresolved by this design and is never counted as evidence that repetition does nothing. The largest fraction of the full-strength difference the interval does exclude is reported.
REPETITION       -- the 6-vs-1 difference excludes zero and is POSITIVE. More sightings of the same total do more. (These two bullets carried the strength pilot run 'same/opposite direction as the full-strength pair' phrasing when this file was first written; the paragraph above already replaced it with the sign of the difference itself, and the bullets are restated here to match the rule that is implemented and was pre-registered. The two readings differ for one member, OLMo-2-32B, whose full-strength pair also falls; it is undefined under the primary installation rule either way.)
SPREADING_COSTS  -- the 6-vs-1 difference excludes zero and is NEGATIVE: the same total spread thinner does LESS. Read together with the ladder's middle rung, whose stacked L2 equals the one-sighting cell's: if that rung is indistinguishable from the one-sighting cell the shape is named L2_MAGNITUDE.
MIXED_NON_MONOTONE -- the endpoints tie but an adjacent pair moves; the shape is named and reported per model, never averaged into a panel number.
UNDEFINED_THIN_CELL_NOT_INSTALLED -- the far end of the constant-total line failed its own installation check, so the line is not measurable there. NOT a null, and never counted with the flat lines: a member whose thinnest cell did not install provides no evidence for the dosage account, however flat its numbers look.
UNDEFINED_REFERENCE_NOT_INSTALLED -- the one-sighting reference cell failed.
UNDEFINED_CELL_NOT_INSTALLED -- some other compared cell failed.
row_reading.magnitude_convention: Injecting k * v at e positions delivers a SUM of per-position magnitudes k * e and a stacked L2 norm k * sqrt(e) * |v|. The constant-total row holds the SUM constant, so its stacked L2 falls as 1/sqrt(e): the six-sighting cell carries 0.408 of the one-sighting cell's L2. Both accountings are reported for every cell, and the verdict names which one it is stated in. The strength ladder at six sightings is what separates them: its middle rung, k = 1/sqrt(6), has the same stacked L2 as one sighting at full strength.
row_reading.magnitude_residual: The correction makes the delivered total equal by construction, and the stage-1 gate checks that within 3 percent before the run proceeds. The residual machinery is kept anyway and reported: every comparison carries the raw paired difference, the measured offset in delivered magnitude between the two cells with the direction it favours, and the same difference recomputed with each cell's slope rescaled to unit delivered magnitude. A pair counts as MOVING only when both the raw and the adjusted difference exclude zero in the same direction. With the offset near zero the two agree by construction; the machinery exists so a residual cannot hide.
row_reading.multiplicity: Each member's verdict reads four bootstrap intervals -- the 6-vs-1 difference and three adjacent pairs -- across seven members, 28 interval decisions in all, and no correction is applied. The rule is asymmetric: REPETITION or SPREADING_COSTS needs ONE interval to exclude zero (about 0.35 spurious calls expected across the panel at 5 percent), while MIXED_NON_MONOTONE triggers on any of three (about one expected). So a panel count of 1 in either category is not read as a per-model finding, and the report says so wherever such a count appears.
row_reading.nonlinearity_scope: The constant-total row changes two things that cannot be separated within a cell: how many positions carry the state, and how strong each one is. If the per-position response saturates or has a threshold, a row difference can come from the strength change rather than from repetition. The run bounds this rather than assuming it away: the ladder gives three per-position strengths at the SAME six sightings, which is a measured per-position dose response at fixed exposure count. Any row verdict is stated together with that curve. Separating a smooth power law from a threshold sitting below the thinnest rung needs finer rungs near the thin end and is OUT OF SCOPE here; it is not claimed either way.

span_rule_shift.note: the same cell (six sightings, full strength) under the corrected span rule minus the legacy rule, paired on shared skeletons. MEASURED and reported; never gated on, because the geometry is exactly what changed.

width_shift.note: the one-sighting cell at full template width minus the same cell under the narrow-span pilot run thin rule, paired on shared skeletons. The two differ in injected width AND in the priming turn, which is the whole change this run makes; MEASURED and reported, never gated on.

retention.note: the fidelity gate drops a session whose steered read moves the unsteered margin too far. Floor skeletons carry 24 random directions each and are dropped if ANY of them fails, so they attrit much harder than main sessions; a probe or choice rank is computed on the skeletons that survived.

prior.note: the strength pilot run own measurements under the LEGACY span rule, quoted for the before/after table. They are not comparable cell-for-cell with this run's corrected geometry and are never used as a gate on anything measured here.

REPETITION       -- the 6-vs-1 difference excludes zero and is POSITIVE. More sightings of the same total do more. (These two bullets carried the strength pilot run 'same/opposite direction as the full-strength pair' phrasing when this file was first written; the paragraph above already replaced it with the sign of the difference itself, and the bullets are restated here to match the rule that is implemented and was pre-registered. The two readings differ for one member, OLMo-2-32B, whose full-strength pair also falls; it is undefined under the primary installation rule either way.)
SPREADING_COSTS  -- the 6-vs-1 difference excludes zero and is NEGATIVE: the same total spread thinner does LESS. Read together with the ladder's middle rung, whose stacked L2 equals the one-sighting cell's: if that rung is indistinguishable from the one-sighting cell the shape is named L2_MAGNITUDE.
MIXED_NON_MONOTONE -- the endpoints tie but an adjacent pair moves; the shape is named and reported per model, never averaged into a panel number.
UNDEFINED_THIN_CELL_NOT_INSTALLED -- the far end of the constant-total line failed its own installation check, so the line is not measurable there. NOT a null, and never counted with the flat lines: a member whose thinnest cell did not install provides no evidence for the dosage account, however flat its numbers look.
UNDEFINED_REFERENCE_NOT_INSTALLED -- the one-sighting reference cell failed.
UNDEFINED_CELL_NOT_INSTALLED -- some other compared cell failed.
row_reading.magnitude_convention: Injecting k * v at e positions delivers a SUM of per-position magnitudes k * e and a stacked L2 norm k * sqrt(e) * |v|. The constant-total row holds the SUM constant, so its stacked L2 falls as 1/sqrt(e): the six-sighting cell carries 0.408 of the one-sighting cell's L2. Both accountings are reported for every cell, and the verdict names which one it is stated in. The strength ladder at six sightings is what separates them: its middle rung, k = 1/sqrt(6), has the same stacked L2 as one sighting at full strength.
row_reading.magnitude_residual: The correction makes the delivered total equal by construction, and the stage-1 gate checks that within 3 percent before the run proceeds. The residual machinery is kept anyway and reported: every comparison carries the raw paired difference, the measured offset in delivered magnitude between the two cells with the direction it favours, and the same difference recomputed with each cell's slope rescaled to unit delivered magnitude. A pair counts as MOVING only when both the raw and the adjusted difference exclude zero in the same direction. With the offset near zero the two agree by construction; the machinery exists so a residual cannot hide.
row_reading.multiplicity: Each member's verdict reads four bootstrap intervals -- the 6-vs-1 difference and three adjacent pairs -- across seven members, 28 interval decisions in all, and no correction is applied. The rule is asymmetric: REPETITION or SPREADING_COSTS needs ONE interval to exclude zero (about 0.35 spurious calls expected across the panel at 5 percent), while MIXED_NON_MONOTONE triggers on any of three (about one expected). So a panel count of 1 in either category is not read as a per-model finding, and the report says so wherever such a count appears.
row_reading.nonlinearity_scope: The constant-total row changes two things that cannot be separated within a cell: how many positions carry the state, and how strong each one is. If the per-position response saturates or has a threshold, a row difference can come from the strength change rather than from repetition. The run bounds this rather than assuming it away: the ladder gives three per-position strengths at the SAME six sightings, which is a measured per-position dose response at fixed exposure count. Any row verdict is stated together with that curve. Separating a smooth power law from a threshold sitting below the thinnest rung needs finer rungs near the thin end and is OUT OF SCOPE here; it is not claimed either way.

retention.note: the fidelity gate drops a session whose steered read moves the unsteered margin too far. Floor skeletons carry 24 random directions each and are dropped if ANY of them fails, so they attrit much harder than main sessions; a probe or choice rank is computed on the skeletons that survived.

prior.note: the strength pilot run own measurements under the LEGACY span rule, quoted for the before/after table. They are not comparable cell-for-cell with this run's corrected geometry and are never used as a gate on anything measured here.
